_comment: API conventions ratchet (Phase 2, spec §2). Enforced by tests/test_api_conventions_ratchet.py; rules documented in docs/internal/reference/API_CONVENTIONS.md. Append a domain to converted_domains in the slice PR that converts it — never before. Every exception needs a route that exists, a known rule id, and a reason a reviewer can argue with.

exceptions.reason: Reset is unconditional and idempotent: no board id to miss, no state in which it refuses, and its one internal failure path is swallowed and logged on purpose so a broken settings store cannot block the wizard reset. Nothing to declare at any status.
Takes no input and reads no resource id — the only failure is 'the display service is not initialized yet', which is a 503 by API_CONVENTIONS.md (dependency down), not a 4xx.
Listing has no failure path: it returns [] for an empty store and cannot 404 or 400, so declaring a 4xx would document an error the endpoint never raises.

No failure mode to declare at any status. It takes no path, query or body parameter and reads process-local config that always exists, so it cannot 400, cannot 404, and raises no HTTPException of its own. The rule now accepts a 5xx, but the only 500 this route can produce is an unhandled bug — true of every route, and documenting it would put noise in the schema rather than a contract.
Parameterless read of the deprecated legacy board view. It projects an empty boards store into defaults rather than failing, so there is no status — 4xx or 5xx — that it deliberately returns.

Parameterless dump of the masked config document, with no HTTPException raised anywhere in the handler. Nothing the caller sends can be wrong and nothing it reads can be missing. The 5xx the widened rule would accept is only the generic unhandled-error case, which is not this route's contract.

Parameterless read of the general settings block, which falls back to defaults when absent. No input to validate, nothing to not-find, and no raise in the handler. Its sibling PUT does declare 422 and 500, because it really can return both.

A verdict endpoint. 'This install is not configured' is the answer at 200 with valid=false, and the handler raises nothing. There is no caller mistake it rejects and no dependency it reports as unavailable.

The whole point of the endpoint is to report connectivity failures in its 200 body; the caller supplies no input to get wrong. The only failure is the diagnostics runner itself blowing up, which is a 500.

Has no client-error path at all: every collaborator it reads (connection info, uptime, cache status, board-configured probe) is defensive and answers with a fallback rather than raising, so the card renders for an unconfigured install too. Declaring a 4xx would document a failure this route cannot produce.

No failure path: an instance with no plugins installed answers an empty list with total 0. It reads the in-process plugin registry, which always exists, and reports availability per entry rather than failing on an unavailable one.

Has no failure path of its own: an instance with no pages answers {"pages": [], "total": 0}. The only 4xx it can produce is the auth middleware's 401, which is applied app-wide and is not this route's contract to declare.
Reports in-memory preview-cache occupancy, which always exists — an empty cache is a valid answer, not an error. Nothing it reads can be missing or unauthorized at the route level.

The only failure path is the 503 raised by _require_plugin_system() when the plugin package did not import — a dependency outage, not a client error. It is declared in responses=; there is no 4xx to declare because no request to this route can be wrong.
The endpoint whose job is to report failures cannot itself fail: with the plugin system down it answers plugin_system_enabled=false and empty maps, which is the correct answer, not an error.

The only failure path is the 503 raised by _require_plugin_system() when the plugin package did not import — a dependency outage, not a client error. It is declared in responses=; there is no 4xx to declare because no request to this route can be wrong.

The only failure path is the 503 raised by _require_plugin_system() when the plugin package did not import — a dependency outage, not a client error. It is declared in responses=; there is no 4xx to declare because no request to this route can be wrong.
Has no failure path at all: with the plugin system down it falls back to the template engine's own variables rather than erroring, because the template editor still has a vocabulary without plugins.

No failure path. The only argument is board_id, and a board-scoped read deliberately falls back to the empty list instead of 404ing (API_CONVENTIONS.md, 'board_id validation: writes 404, reads fall back'); board_id=* is a documented wildcard, not an id.

No failure path. It reports whatever is on the board right now — manual page, scheduled page, or nothing — and every collection resolution failure is caught and reported as null rather than raised, because a dashboard poll must not error out over a collection that cannot resolve.
No failure path. An unknown board_id deliberately answers the global default rather than 404 — the same read/write asymmetry, decided in #1888 and documented in API_CONVENTIONS.md.
No failure path. An unknown board_id deliberately answers false rather than 404 — the same read/write asymmetry, decided in #1888 and documented in API_CONVENTIONS.md.

Reads the bundled staff-picks/picks.json and degrades a missing file to [] on purpose, so a caller can never see a 4xx from it. The per-pick 404 lives on GET /staff-picks/{pick_id}/share, which declares it.

Probe endpoint (API_CONVENTIONS.md, "Status codes"): an unreachable Docker Hub or GitHub is a verdict about something else, reported at 200 in the declared UpdateCheckResponse.error field. Nothing the caller sends can make this route 4xx.

Read-only report with no failure path: it cannot 404, 400 or 409, so declaring a 4xx would document an error the endpoint never raises. An unreachable sidecar is reported as updater_available=false, not as an error.
No failure path: the function table is a module-level constant in src/templates/expressions.py with no input and no I/O, so nothing the caller controls can make it fail.

No failure path: it reads the in-process template engine and plugin registry, both of which always exist. An install with no plugins answers empty catalogs alongside the static colour/symbol/filter tables — an empty answer, not an error.

Read-only report with no failure path: it cannot 404, 400 or 409, so declaring a 4xx would document an error the endpoint never raises. It reads two env vars and one /proc file, and reports None when the file is absent.
Same as GET /cache-status: no body, no path parameter, and the only failure is the uninitialized display service, which is a 503.

Same declared verdict contract as POST /config/board/test (#1887): 'that enablement token is not valid' is the board's answer at 200 through EnableLocalApiResponse. The SSRF and host-validation rejections stayed 400 and the unexpected-exception path stayed 500 when Task 10a fixed this handler.

Declared probe contract (#1887, Task 10a): the endpoint's job is to report what the board said, so 'your key was rejected' is the requested answer at 200 through BoardTestResponse, not a transport failure. Preconditions the server rejects before probing (missing credential, unsafe host) really are 400, and unanticipated errors really are 500 — tests/test_status_code_correctness.py pins both. Making the upstream verdicts 4xx would tell the wizard the request was malformed when it was not.
No body and no path parameter, so nothing the caller sends can be wrong. It answers 503 when the display service is not initialized and 500 when the forced send pass reports a failure reason.

Same 503-only shape as its siblings, plus a deliberate partial-success contract: a bulk update of N plugins reports per-plugin outcomes in `failed` at 200, because collapsing them into one status code would throw away which plugin failed and why.

The only failure path is the 503 raised by _require_plugin_system() when the plugin package did not import — a dependency outage, not a client error. It is declared in responses=; there is no 4xx to declare because no request to this route can be wrong.

Three returns inside except blocks, all deliberate. Two serve the last good options with stale=true when the provider times out or throws, so a settings form mid-edit keeps its picker instead of blanking. The third turns OptionsUnavailable ("no API key yet") into a 200 with an error hint, because that is the expected state while the user is still filling in the very field the credential goes in — a 4xx there would surface a failed-request toast for a form that is simply incomplete.

No failure path. It is a read of existing schedules with an optional board_id, which falls back to the empty set; an inconsistent schedule set is the 200 verdict this endpoint exists to report, not an error.

Every failure mode is upstream: the fiestaupdater sidecar is absent (503), rejects our shared token (500) or errors (502). There is no request a client could send that this route answers 4xx to, and all three codes it does raise are declared in responses=.
